content: The presence of HIV and the attitudes and counseling messages of health workers in Lilongwe, Malawi, were discussed in a publication in the International Breastfeeding Journal in 2006. The article highlights the importance of addressing HIV in the context of breastfeeding practices and the role of health workers in providing appropriate counseling. The World Health Organization (WHO) has developed guidelines for counseling women to improve breastfeeding practices. These guidelines were created with input from a steering group of experts in maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health, as well as nutrition and reproductive health. Key contributors include Dr. Samira Aboubaker, Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Dr. Meghan Bohren, Dr. Laurence Grummer-Strawn, Dr. Juan Pablo Peña-Rosas, Dr. Pura Rayco-Solon, and Dr. Nigel Rollins, among others. Each expert brought specialized knowledge in areas such as breastfeeding, maternal and child health, nutrition, and HIV. The guideline development group included professionals with expertise in neonatology, lactation management, maternal and child health policies, and breastfeeding program design. Notable members include Dr. Ebunoula A. Adejuyigbe, Professor Abdou-Rahmane Diparidé Agbèrè, Dr. Rifat Nisar Ashraf, Dr. Teresita González de Cosio, Dr. Elsa RJ Giugliani, Dr. Marianne Nishani Lucas, Ms. Marie McGrath, Dr. Purnima Menon, Professor Rafael Pérez-Escamilla, Dr. Vanessa Aline Rouzier, Ms. Randa Jarudi Saadeh, Professor Mohamadou Guélaye Sall, Dr. Felicity M. Savage, Dr. Maria Asuncion A. Silvestre, Dr. Olena Starets, Professor Mark Tomlinson, Ms. Terrie Wefwafwa, and Ms. Ruikan Yang. Their expertise spans areas such as breastfeeding counseling, maternal and child health, HIV transmission, and nutrition policies. The systematic review team, which contributed to the evidence base for the guidelines, included experts such as Stephen Macgillivray, Alison McFadden, and Emma Sacks. Their work synthesized evidence to inform the recommendations. External reviewers, including Dr. Maryse Arendt, Dr. JP Dadhich, Ms. Iona Macnab, and Mr. Roger Mathisen, provided additional perspectives. Their affiliations and contributions are acknowledged, though their participation does not imply endorsement of the recommendations. The guidelines emphasize the importance of evidence-based counseling to improve breastfeeding practices, particularly in contexts where HIV and other health challenges may impact maternal and child health outcomes.
